runtime_status: release-candidate; Linux/static/artifact gates pass locally; Windows PowerShell 5.1 provider-sync runtime gate is wired into Windows CI and remains authoritative until exercised there or on the target machine
notes: v7.9.5: capability profiles. Seven MCP servers evaluated from an external capability review are shipped as named profiles in BUNDLED-TOOLS/PROFILES.json rather than registered globally -- Serena, Chrome DevTools, shadcn, Supabase, Blender, Godot and Unity. The reason is measurable: TOOLS/Test-McpHandshake.ps1 ran the real initialize -> tools/list exchange against this machine's live configs and found 188 tool schemas riding in context on every turn of every Claude session, against 136 for Codex and 90 for Grok. Skills are lazy and MCP schemas are not, so the profile router wires a server only when the project shows its markers and the machine satisfies its requirements, and prints the missing prerequisite otherwise instead of writing an entry that fails on first call. Both config writers now share TOOLS/V7-Mcp-Write.ps1: every config bug this pack has shipped was a bug in one of three config shapes that the other two did not have. The new gate TESTS/Test-McpProfiles.ps1 caught two on its first run -- PowerShell unrolls a single-element array on return, so a one-argument server would have been written as "args": "blender-mcp"; and -CheckOnly deleted the entries it claimed it would only report on. The handshake probe then found a live defect no static check could: Codex still held @playwright/mcp@latest with no -y, so npx blocked on an install prompt and the server never answered initialize. Update-V5GrokMcpBlock -SkipIfPresent compared only the command, and every npx server has the same command -- so a pin added in a later release could never reach a machine that already had the entry. It now compares the args. Unreal MCP was evaluated and not shipped: last upstream commit 2025-06-06. 144 canonical skills across 5 provider trees.
